step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture illustrates ContentWise's machine learning workflow on AWS. The process begins with data scientists interacting with Amazon ECR to store custom Docker images and utilizing SageMaker Notebooks for orchestrating the ML lifecycle. The overall SageMaker service orchestrates these components. SageMaker Training uses the Docker images from ECR and datasets stored in an S3 bucket (S3 Dataset) to produce a trained model. This model artifact (SageMaker Model) is then saved to another S3 bucket (S3 Model). For real-time inference, the trained model from S3 is deployed via a SageMaker Endpoint. A Lambda function acts as an intermediary, called by the production application hosted on EC2, to invoke the SageMaker Endpoint for predictions. Lambda then enriches these raw predictions before returning them to the EC2 application. All core AWS services for ML and application (SageMaker components, Lambda, EC2) are conceptually within a VPC, as depicted by the bounding box.

graph.name: ContentWise Machine Learning Workflow on AWS
graph.categories: Machine Learning, AI/ML, Data Processing, Analytics
graph.notes: ContentWise uses AWS to train, deploy, and serve machine learning models for content personalization. The workflow leverages SageMaker for model development, ECR for custom Docker images, S3 for data storage, and Lambda/EC2 for production integration. The diagram shows the flow from data scientists pushing images and interacting with notebooks, through training and model storage, to the final real-time inference serving via an endpoint and application layer.

nodes.name: Data Scientist
nodes.notes: Represents data scientists who manage the machine learning workflow, including pushing Docker images and interacting with SageMaker notebooks.

nodes.name: VPC
nodes.notes: The virtual private cloud that contains the core AWS services for the machine learning and application infrastructure.

nodes.name: ECR Registry
nodes.notes: Stores custom Docker images required for SageMaker training and endpoint deployment.

nodes.name: S3 Dataset
nodes.notes: Amazon S3 bucket used to store input datasets for model training.

nodes.name: S3 Model
nodes.notes: Amazon S3 bucket used to store trained machine learning model artifacts.

nodes.name: SageMaker Service
nodes.notes: The overarching Amazon SageMaker service, which orchestrates various ML tasks from data analysis to model deployment.

nodes.name: SageMaker Notebook
nodes.notes: SageMaker Notebook instances used by data scientists to prototype, analyze data, and orchestrate model training.

nodes.name: SageMaker Training
nodes.notes: The training job component within SageMaker that performs model training using specified Docker images and datasets.

nodes.name: SageMaker Model
nodes.notes: The output artifact of a SageMaker training job, representing the trained machine learning model.

nodes.name: SageMaker Endpoint
nodes.notes: A real-time inference endpoint hosted by SageMaker, serving predictions from the deployed model.

nodes.name: Lambda Function
nodes.notes: An AWS Lambda function used to enrich raw predictions from the SageMaker endpoint before delivering them to the production application.

nodes.name: EC2 Production App
nodes.notes: Amazon EC2 instances hosting the ContentWise production application, which consumes the enriched machine learning predictions.

edges.notes: Data Scientist pushes custom Docker images to ECR.
Data Scientist interacts with SageMaker Notebooks for experimentation and orchestration.
SageMaker Notebooks initiate the model training process.
SageMaker Training pulls custom Docker images from ECR.
SageMaker Training accesses datasets from S3 Dataset bucket.
SageMaker Training produces a trained model artifact.
The trained model artifact is stored in the S3 Model bucket.
The stored model from S3 is used to create or update the SageMaker Endpoint.
The EC2 production application calls the Lambda function for predictions.
Lambda invokes the SageMaker Endpoint to get raw predictions.
SageMaker Endpoint returns raw predictions to Lambda.
Lambda enriches predictions and returns them to the EC2 production application.
